```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 150
)
```

Get the CANHR colors in R and use them with ggplot2 and base R graphics.

```{r}
library(canhrcolors)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Getting colors

`canhrcolors()` returns the full palette as hex codes. Give it one or more
color names to get just those colors.

```{r}
canhrcolors()
canhrcolors("blue")
canhrcolors(c("deep teal", "warm berry"))
```

## ggplot2

`scale_color_canhr()` and `scale_fill_canhr()` color groups in palette order,
and `theme_canhr()` styles the titles, text and grid lines. The examples use
data that come with R and ggplot2.

### Scatter plot

```{r scatter, fig.cap = "Highway mileage by engine size in the mpg data, colored by drive type."}
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, color = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_canhr(labels = c("4WD", "Front", "Rear")) +
  theme_canhr() +
  labs(
    title = "Fuel economy by engine size",
    x = "Engine displacement (litres)",
    y = "Highway miles per gallon",
    color = "Drive"
  )
```

### Bar chart

```{r bar, fig.cap = "Number of cars in each class in the mpg data."}
ggplot(mpg, aes(class, fill = class)) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_canhr() +
  theme_canhr() +
  labs(title = "Cars by class", x = NULL, y = "Number of cars")
```

### Box plot

```{r boxplot, fig.cap = "Petal length for the three species in the iris data."}
ggplot(iris, aes(Species, Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_canhr() +
  theme_canhr() +
  labs(title = "Petal length by species", x = NULL, y = "Petal length (cm)")
```

### One color

Use a single color by name.

```{r histogram, fig.cap = "Minutes between Old Faithful eruptions in the faithful data."}
ggplot(faithful, aes(waiting)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = canhrcolors("blue"), color = "white") +
  theme_canhr() +
  labs(
    title = "Time between Old Faithful eruptions",
    x = "Minutes",
    y = "Number of eruptions"
  )
```

A plot that needs more colors than the palette has gets a warning and draws
the extra groups in grey.

## Base R graphics

The colors work anywhere R accepts a color.

```{r base-r, fig.cap = "Petal width against petal length in the iris data, drawn with base R."}
pal <- canhrcolors()[1:3]
plot(Petal.Width ~ Petal.Length, data = iris, col = pal[Species], pch = 19,
     xlab = "Petal length (cm)", ylab = "Petal width (cm)")
legend("topleft", legend = levels(iris$Species), col = pal, pch = 19, bty = "n")
```

## Color reference

|--------------|-------------------------------|-----------|
| Blue         | `canhrcolors("blue")`         | `#236192` |
| Gold         | `canhrcolors("gold")`         | `#FFCD00` |
| Green        | `canhrcolors("green")`        | `#71984A` |
| Orange       | `canhrcolors("orange")`       | `#DF6A2E` |
| Cyan         | `canhrcolors("cyan")`         | `#87D1E6` |
| Magenta      | `canhrcolors("magenta")`      | `#F45197` |
| Dark Blue    | `canhrcolors("dark blue")`    | `#111C4E` |
| Brown        | `canhrcolors("brown")`        | `#774D28` |
| Dark Grey    | `canhrcolors("dark grey")`    | `#66665D` |
| Custard      | `canhrcolors("custard")`      | `#F6DFA4` |

| Deep Teal    | `canhrcolors("deep teal")`    | `#165B63` |
